title: Taxonomy
description: DataViews term manager for any taxonomy. `config.taxonomy` selects which taxonomy to manage; defaults to `category`.

variant.description: Optional DataView variant id. v2 back-compat: when the v3 compiler synthesizes a screen from a v2 route, `config.variant` stays on `screen.config.variant` and the resolver's step-3 manifest-inference path reads it directly to reach `settings.dataViews.taxonomy.<taxonomy>.<variant>`.

documentation.purpose: DataViews-driven manager for any WordPress taxonomy. Defaults to `category`; rebind via the `taxonomy` config key for `post_tag` or any custom taxonomy. Authors can list (with search, sort, pagination), create, edit (in a modal with name / slug / description / parent fields), and bulk delete terms. Hierarchical taxonomies (e.g. category) render rows in true depth-first tree order — parent immediately above its indented children — under the default name-ascending first-page view with no active search, when the whole tree fits on one page (with a visually-hidden `Level N` for assistive tech); other sorts / pages / searches, or a tree larger than one page, fall back to flat REST order with no indentation (larger trees paginate alphabetically). They also offer an indented parent picker on add/edit; the site default category is badged and protected from deletion. Replaces wp-admin's `edit-tags.php` for the configured taxonomy.

reads.purpose: Resolved DataView doc — fields, default view, default layouts, actions. Read via `useDataView(screenId)`; baseline ships in `app.json#dataView` bound to `(taxonomy, category)` and is injected post-merge by `inject_app_baselines`. Other taxonomies (`post_tag`, custom) consume cascade-only entries or filter overrides.
Term rows in the DataViews table.

Reads the taxonomy's `hierarchical` flag (GET /wp/v2/taxonomies/{taxonomy}) to decide whether to render the parent-indented tree + parent picker (issue #115). Loading returns null → defaults to flat so the table paints without waiting.

Full flat term set (per_page 100, `_fields: id,name,parent`), fetched only for hierarchical taxonomies, to build the depth tree + the indented parent-picker options client-side independent of the paged/sorted/searched list (issue #115).
Reads `default_category` (category taxonomy only) to badge the default term and make it delete-ineligible (issue #116). WordPress refuses to delete the default category server-side.

writes.purpose: Add a new term via the Add new modal (name / slug / description, plus `parent` for hierarchical taxonomies).
Edit an existing term (name / slug / description, plus `parent` for hierarchical taxonomies — the edited term excludes itself from the parent options to prevent a self-parent cycle).
Bulk-delete terms permanently (`force: true` — taxonomies have no trash).

states.renders: Table of terms with row + bulk actions.

states.when: taxonomy is hierarchical (taxonomyRecord.hierarchical) && allTerms resolved && view sorted by name asc on page 1 with no active search AND the whole tree fits on one page (totalItems <= perPage)
states.renders: The page's rows are reordered client-side from the flat REST (alphabetical) order into the term-tree depth-first sequence so a parent renders immediately above its indented children (true wp-admin order). Name column rows are indented by client-computed depth with a visually-hidden `Level N` (screen-reader-text); no `role=treeitem`/`aria-level` (orphaned inside the DataViews table). Flat taxonomies — or any non-default sort / later page / active search / tree larger than one page — keep the flat REST order with no indentation and no depth announcement (REST pages alphabetically, so a multi-page tree could float an indented child whose parent lands on a later page; larger trees paginate flat).
A neutral `Default` Badge beside the term name; the row's Delete action is ineligible (hidden).
Modal with name / slug / description fields populated from the term, plus a `parent` integer picker (indented elements) for hierarchical taxonomies.
Same modal with empty fields and Add term button.
Save button shows loading spinner; inputs stay editable.
Confirm modal with destructive primary button.

interactions.effect: Open the term modal in create mode.

interactions.trigger: Click row name or Edit action
interactions.effect: Open the term modal in edit mode pre-filled from `item.rawRecord`.
`saveEntityRecord('taxonomy', taxonomy, payload)`; on success: success snackbar + invalidate `getEntityRecords` + close modal. On failure: error notice (dismissible).

Open confirm modal; on confirm `deleteEntityRecord(..., { force: true })` for each item + invalidate + success snackbar. The default category (issue #116) is delete-ineligible — its Delete action is hidden, so it can't enter a bulk batch.

interactions.trigger: Pick a Parent in the term modal (hierarchical taxonomies)
interactions.effect: `parent` (integer) is included in the save payload; on add the term nests under the chosen parent, on edit it reparents. The edited term excludes itself from the options.
Local `view` updates; queryArgs recomputes; records refetch.

a11y.focus-management: DataViews owns focus inside the table. The legacy `Modal` traps focus; on close, DataViews restores focus to the trigger.

constraints.note: Taxonomies have no trash. `deleteEntityRecord` must pass `{ force: true }` or the request 400s.
Uses legacy `Modal` from `@wordpress/components` because WPDS 0.12's Dialog is not a clean port for complex form modals.
Uses legacy `TextareaControl` — WPDS 0.12 has no TextareaControl port.
Both create + update + delete must call `invalidateResolution('getEntityRecords', ['taxonomy', taxonomy])` — `saveEntityRecord` does not bust the parent query.

Term `name`/`description` may contain HTML entities (`&`, `'`). Pass through `decodeEntities` before rendering — both in the list cell AND when seeding the edit modal from `rawRecord`, otherwise the input shows the encoded form and re-saving double-encodes. Mirrors wp-admin's `wp_specialchars_decode` display.

The full-term fetch that drives the tree + parent picker is capped at `per_page: 100` (REST max). Trees larger than 100 terms degrade gracefully — terms beyond the cap fall outside the indented set rather than breaking. Pagination of the tree fetch is a future enhancement (issue #115).

Default-category protection (issue #116) works only for `category` — `default_category` is the one default-term option exposed at GET /wp/v2/settings. Custom hierarchical taxonomies' `default_term_{taxonomy}` is NOT REST-readable, so their default term can't be pre-protected; the REST 500 still surfaces on delete.

design-system-leakage.purpose: DataViews + DataForm components, field descriptor shape. Table view with sort/pagination/actions.
Header, modal layout, indented name cell, Add-new icon, and the `Default` term Badge.
Destructive confirm action, modal container, multiline description input — WPDS 0.12 gaps.
Success / error notices for create / update / delete flows. The canonical shell notices contract — a non-WPDS rebuild must mirror it.
Add-new toolbar icon. Row + delete icons resolve through the kernel icon registry (`pencil`, `trash`).
